item.title: What Israel wants from an Iran peace deal: No enrichment, missile limits and strict enforcement
item.description: Israel wants Iran to stop enrichment, dismantle underground nuclear sites, restrict missiles and cut ties to Hamas and Hezbollah, experts say.

item.title: Middle East war live: Trump says Iran war will be 'over quickly'
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Wednesday evening that he believed the war in Iran would be "over quickly" but threatened to resume his bombardment of the country if negotiations fell apart. Earlier that day the US military said it had shot at an Iranian oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman as it tried to breach the US blockade of Iranian ports. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

item.title: Israel strikes Beirut's southern suburbs, targeted 'top Hezbollah commander'
item.description: Israel on Wednesday unleashed the first air strikes in weeks on Beirut’s southern suburbs. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the attack, saying a top commander of the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group was targeted in the operation. Read our liveblog to see how all the day's events unfolded.

item.title: UAE’s ruling royal family benefits from more than €71m in EU farming subsidies
item.description:
Al Nahyans’ control over farmland in Europe has meant they receive proportion of payments to farms

The United Arab Emirates’ ruling royal family is benefiting from tens of millions in EU subsidies to grow crops destined for the Gulf, it can be revealed.

A cross-border investigation by DeSmog and shared with the Guardian found subsidiaries controlled by the Al Nahyans collected more than €71m (£61m) in six years for farmland it controls in Romania, Italy and Spain.

item.title: 100 years on Earth: celebrating David Attenborough’s birthday – podcast
item.description:
To celebrate Sir David Attenborough’s centenary, Madeleine Finlay catches up with natural history writer Patrick Barkham, who has met the celebrated presenter. They explore how the natural world has changed in the century that Attenborough has been on Earth, and how his programming has reflected his growing commitment to highlighting the devastating impacts of the climate crisis on nature and biodiversity
